source_request: 시각 의미 데이터와 후보 데이터에 반영해줘. 그 다음 스킬의 최신 버전을 사용하여 독립된 서브에이전트 3개에서 각각 서로 다른 컨셉으로 이번에 반영한 주제가 이미지에 실제로 반영되는지까지 테스트할 수 있는 랜덤한 복잡한 컨셉을 정하여 테스트케이스를 마련하고 첨부한 이미지를 활용하여 프롬프트 작성하고 이미지 생성하도록 하여 잘 반영되었는지 테스트해줘.
interpreted_intent: Requester asks independent complex randomized concepts using the attached image to test the newly integrated fashion-fit topic. All letterpress-shop circumstances, charcoal tailoring, precise fit choices, time, mood and camera staging are agent-owned realizations. Selected seeded combination: a first-exhibition letterpress workshop at violet dusk, a proof drying on an improvised cord, and a privately amused pause after solving limited drying space. The photograph should make her warm, particular presence and the tactile relationship of body, jacket and long trousers legible together. A static wardrobe catalog and a dramatic arrival scene were considered; this practical waiting moment gives the tailoring a coherent reason to be present while keeping its boundaries visible. Saved sensual=1 supports subtle personal attraction, fetish=0 and surreal=0 add no treatment, creativity=1 keeps the combination materially ordinary.
subject: A woman using only the attached image visible face and hair cues; charcoal jacket and matching trousers are agent choices.
setting: Working letterpress shop at violet dusk; this setting is an agent invention.
event: A pause in layered work clothes while a freshly printed proof dries; the print task is agent invention.
visual_priorities: Body-to-jacket relation: shoulder seam, sleeve wrist endpoint, cropped front and generous lower jacket ease remain readable together.
Same-trouser continuity: visible natural-waist band, freely hanging thigh and knee fabric, and a soft shoe-top break on long straight legs.
A hanging damp proof, press rollers and spare clip connect her waiting and amused attention to the improvised drying solution.
Visible face and short bob guide the person, with warm cheek light supporting her private half-smile in cool workshop depth.
baseline_prompt_en: A photographic study of garment fit centers on a photographed woman wearing clothing with visible fit. She pauses between practical tasks. The supplied reference guides her visible face and hair: a short dark brown bob, airy fringe separating into fine strands, dark rounded eyes and a softly tapered face with natural rose lips. Her quiet, attentive presence and a small amused half-smile make the portrait feel personal. She stands in a working letterpress shop at violet dusk, just before the first print exhibition. A newly pulled cream proof sheet with still-damp charcoal ink hangs from two wooden clips on a short improvised drying cord behind her, stretching from a type cabinet to a metal post. The open stack of similar blank sheets and inked press rollers explain what has just happened. She has solved the drying-space problem with this awkward little line and now waits, looking toward the hanging sheet with private amusement. Her right hand holds one spare wooden clip at upper chest height, elbow close to her torso; her left arm falls naturally beside her hip, with the hand relaxed and visible. Her shoulders are level and both feet rest fully on the worn wooden floor, the right foot a small step forward. She wears a short charcoal brushed-wool single-breasted tailored jacket over an ivory ribbed knit and matching long straight trousers. The jacket shoulder seam meets the outer shoulder point, its sleeve hanging in a smooth vertical line to the wrist. Its fronts meet at one fastened button near the hem while the lower body of the jacket has generous space around her torso; the wool forms shallow vertical folds instead of taut diagonals at that button. The jacket hem ends just above the trouser waistband, leaving the waistband visible across the front. The trouser waistband follows her natural waist closely, then the fabric hangs freely through the thighs and knees. Each straight trouser leg reaches the top of a dark leather loafer with one soft fold above the instep, and the rear hem stays clear of the floor. The broad lapels, dry wool nap, pale ribbing and polished shoes produce distinct tactile rhythms; her body feels present inside the tailoring rather than disappearing into a garment silhouette. A dim amber task lamp warms her left cheek and the jacket edge, while the high window gives the workshop its cool violet depth. The coat and waist remain readable against a light plaster wall; the old press, type drawers, cord and cream paper stay softer and subordinate. Photograph her full length from head to both soles in a three-quarter frontal view, the camera at lower-chest height and several steps away. Keep her entire jacket, waistband, both trouser legs and shoes plainly visible, with the press set behind and to the side. The modest perspective, calm eye line and material detail create an intimate environmental fashion photograph whose meaning comes from the practical waiting moment.
